content: Given the adjacency matrix $A_{N \times N}$ of the graph obtained as described previously, let us define the diagonal matrix $D=\text{diag}(\mathbf {d})$ , where $\mathbf {d}=A \mathbf {1}$ is the degree vector. The random walk Laplacian matrix is defined as $L_\text{RW}=I_N-D^{-1}A$ where $I_N$ is the identity matrix of size $N$ , and the transition matrix (or kernel) of the associated continuous-time Markov process is $P(t)=e^{-t L_\text{RW}}, \, t>0$ BIBREF10 . For each partition, a binary membership matrix $H_{N \times C}$ maps the $N$ nodes into $C$ clusters. We can then define the $D=\text{diag}(\mathbf {d})$0 clustered autocovariance matrix:
